title: Everyday routine
intro: Most of this unit is reflexive, because Spanish marks actions you do to yourself: despertarse, levantarse, bañarse, acostarse. The reflexive pronoun is not optional — levantar without it means to lift something else.

entries.note: despertar without se means to wake someone else: despierta a tu hermano.

ex.es: Me despierto a las seis sin despertador.
ex.en: I wake up at six without an alarm.

entries.en: to get up, to stand up
entries.note: levantar alone is to lift or raise something.

ex.en: He gets up very late on Sundays.
I slept eight hours straight.
He fell asleep on the sofa.

entries.en: to go to bed, to lie down

ex.en: I go to bed before midnight.

entries.en: to have a bath; to have a shower
entries.note: In much of Latin America bañarse covers showering too.

ex.es: El niño se baña antes de cenar.
ex.en: The boy has a bath before dinner.
I shower in five minutes.

entries.note: Asking ¿dónde está el baño? is the polite way to ask for the toilet.

ex.en: Where is the bathroom?
She had a long bath.

entries.note: el peine is the comb; el cepillo the brush.

ex.en: Comb your hair before you go out.

entries.note: la barba is a beard; el bigote a moustache.

ex.en: He shaves every other day.

entries.note: poner el despertador is to set the alarm.

ex.en: I didn't hear the alarm.

entries.note: One verb where English needs three words. Same with almorzar and cenar.

ex.en: We have breakfast together every day.

entries.note: el descanso is a rest or a break.

ex.es: Descansa un rato, llevas horas trabajando.
ex.en: Rest for a while, you've been working for hours.

entries.note: el turno is your turn or a shift at work. me toca a mí means it's my turn.

ex.en: Wait your turn, please.

entries.note: See unit 24. In routine contexts se me olvidó is the everyday form.

ex.es: Se me olvidó el almuerzo en casa.
ex.en: I left my lunch at home.

entries.en: to turn off; to turn on, to light
entries.warn: Frequently swapped in word lists. apagar is off, encender is on. prender is the everyday word for on in Latin America.

ex.en: Turn the light off when you leave.
Turn the television on.

entries.note: Past participles: abierto, cerrado — the words on every shop door.

ex.en: Open the window, it's hot.
Lock the door.

entries.note: See unit 2. Together they cover most of what you do with lost keys.

ex.en: I'm looking for my glasses.
I found them in the car.

entries.note: la pasta de dientes is toothpaste; lavarse los dientes to brush your teeth.

ex.en: I forgot my toothbrush.

ex.es: Hay toallas limpias en el baño.
ex.en: There are clean towels in the bathroom.

entries.note: el tiempo libre is free time in general; los ratos libres odd moments.

ex.en: I read in my spare time.

entries.note: For late as an adjective use atrasado or con retraso: el tren viene atrasado.

ex.en: We arrived late again.

ex.es: Salimos temprano para evitar el tráfico.
ex.en: We left early to avoid the traffic.
